_what: What a picture is FOR. One row per purpose, and the row is the only thing that differs between an email hero, an ad frame and a page section — the models, the prompting structure and the context structure are identical for all of them. A purpose not on this list is REFUSED, naming the real ids (the element library's own rule, components/elements).
_why: the owner, 2026-09-21: "create a component for just image production that works regardless of whatever workflow it's in. That way, we go through the same models, the same prompting structures, and the same context structures to develop these images out for any of the assets that we create." Before this, an email hero was made one way (tools/email-production/simple_email.py) and an ad frame another (tools/image-production/static), and the two disagreed about the frame, the reference and the judge.
_curator: the owner. A new purpose is a row here, never a branch in code.

_fields.name: what we call it
_fields.aspect: the default frame, when the request names none
_fields.people: true when a person is normally in frame, false when not, "maybe" when it depends on the direction — read by the model route, never by a caller
_fields.product_reference: none | optional | required — whether the REAL product photo is passed in as a reference so the product is ours and not redrawn
_fields.words: never | when_asked — whether words may be rendered inside the frame
_fields.frame: the purpose's own line in the prompt skeleton, slotted at {purpose_frame}
_fields.safe_zone: true when the frame will be cropped in feed and the standing safe-zone clause applies
_fields.judge: extra judge tests this purpose always runs, beyond the standing ones

email-hero.name: Email hero
email-hero.what: The picture under the headline at the top of an email. It has to say what the headline says, at 600px wide, on a phone.
email-hero.frame: A wide photograph for the top of an email. It is seen small, on a phone, above the copy — one clear subject, read in half a second, nothing that only works at full size.
email-hero.source: tools/email-production/simple_email.py make_pictures() — the hero job, and its "A wide photograph for the top of an email" line, verbatim

email-offer.name: Email offer picture
email-offer.what: The product picture beside the offer and the button. Made FROM the real product photo, never drawn from a description.
email-offer.frame: A wide photograph of the product, for the offer block of an email, above the button.
email-offer.source: tools/email-production/simple_email.py — the offer job, which is the one place the real product photo was already passed in as a reference

ad.name: Static ad frame
ad.what: A paid frame. It ships to a feed, so the frame shape and what survives the crop are part of the job.
ad.frame: A single advertising frame, made to stop a scroll and to be understood before it is read.
judge: The words and the picture are one idea: a stranger who reads the words on the ad and looks at the picture understands why that picture is there, and the words make sense on one read. FAIL a picture whose words are about something the picture does not show, or read as nonsense (the owner, 2026-10-23).
ad.source: tools/image-production/static — the static-ad tool this component was extracted from

page-section.name: Landing-page section picture
page-section.what: The picture inside one section of a landing page, beside that section's copy.
page-section.frame: A wide photograph for one section of a landing page, sitting beside that section's own words and never repeating them.
page-section.source: lab/owner/pages — the page machine is the caller this row is declared for; it has not run through here yet

video-still.name: Scene still
video-still.what: One generated frame standing for one scene of a video, so every scene has a picture.
video-still.frame: A single frame from a scene, as a camera in the room would have caught it — a moment, not a poster.
video-still.source: tools/video-teardown/machine/frames.py — stage 6 generates a frame per scene; that tool is unchanged and this row is declared for the day it is switched over

product-shot.name: Product alone
product-shot.what: The product on a controlled ground, with nothing else in frame.
product-shot.frame: The product alone on a controlled ground. Nothing else is in frame and nothing else is being said.
judge: The product occupies the frame as the only subject. FAIL if a second object, a hand, a person or a background scene competes with it.
product-shot.source: tools/image-production/static/style-packs.json `studio-object` — the register this purpose exists to serve

email-key-visual.name: Email key visual
email-key-visual.what: The picture an email opens on: a designed key visual made to stop the scroll, the way a Halloween email became an 80s horror movie poster with the product as its hero. It carries the email's concept at full scale.
email-key-visual.frame: A designed key visual for the top of an email: a borrowed format at full scale (a movie poster, a magazine cover, a flyer's front page, a TV title card, a gift reveal), dramatic, celebratory and finished like a campaign, with the real product as its star. Seen on a phone, so one bold idea read in half a second; any title the format carries is large and spelled exactly as given.
email-key-visual.source: the owner, 2026-10-17: the email design line's picture types ("the design and images themselves need to feel like a blow out too"); called by tools/email-production/design/line.py

email-gift.name: Email gift picture
email-gift.what: A real product made into the moment's object: wrapped, tagged, in the bag, under the tree, in the stocking. One product per picture, so a set is shown, never listed.
email-gift.frame: A styled square photograph of one real product turned into this moment's object (wrapped, tagged, nestled in tissue, under the tree), rich and celebratory, the product unmistakable and exactly itself.
email-gift.source: the owner, 2026-10-17: the email design line's picture types ("the design and images themselves need to feel like a blow out too"); called by tools/email-production/design/line.py

email-story.name: Email story picture
email-story.what: A supporting picture inside an email: a real moment from the reader's day, documentary and true, that carries one line of the argument.
email-story.frame: A documentary photograph from the reader's own day, natural light, unstaged, one clear subject read on a phone.
email-story.source: the owner, 2026-10-17: the email design line's picture types ("the design and images themselves need to feel like a blow out too"); called by tools/email-production/design/line.py

icon.name: Icon or character
icon.what: One illustrated icon or character for an app, game or site, on a plain ground so its background can be removed.
icon.frame: One centered subject on a plain flat ground, with nothing else in frame, readable at 64 pixels.
judge: The icon is one clear subject, centered, with a plain ground. FAIL if a scene, text or a second subject competes with it.
icon.source: added for app and game icon sets
